sentences.transcript: Memphis by Gordon Mel Herb Hillman, red for liverbox .org
by Noelle Vox.
Why should I sing of my present?
It is nothing to near you.
Rather I dream of Dixie and Thai ships on the old bayou.
Rather I dream of my packets and the lazy river days.
Rather I dream of my levee and the crimson sunset haze.
Rather I dream of my triumphs of the days that are long gone by.
Rather I dream of flame -tipped stacks against the saffron sky.
Of level lawns of toque -as.
Of level fields of jade.
Of the rambling pillared mansions.
That my father's father's made.
Why should I sing of my present?
It is nothing to you or me.
But the river road.
The great road.
The high road to the sea.
I, that is worth the dreaming.
I, that was worth the pain.
Send me back my river and I shall wake again.
End of poem.
